abstract_sentences.text: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with the diverse spectrum of human values remains a central challenge: preference-based methods often fail to capture deeper motivational principles.

abstract_sentences.text: Value-based approaches offer a more principled path, yet three gaps persist: extraction often ignores hierarchical structure, evaluation detects presence but not calibrated intensity, and steerability of LLMs at controlled intensities remains insufficiently understood.

evidence.anchor: Value-based approaches offer a more principled path, yet three gaps persist: extraction of

abstract_sentences.text: To address these limitations, we introduce VALUEFLOW, a unified framework that spans extraction, evaluation, and steering with calibrated intensity control.

evidence.anchor: To address these limitations, we introduce VALUEFLOW, a unified framework that spans extra

abstract_sentences.text: The framework integrates three components: (i) HiVES, a hierarchical value embedding space that captures intra- and cross-theory value structure; (ii) the Value Intensity DataBase (VIDB), a large-scale resource of value-labeled texts with intensity estimates derived from ranking-based aggregation; and (iii) an anchor-based evaluator that produces consistent intensity scores for model outputs by ranking them against VIDB panels.

experimental_design.name: Paper research questions
experimental_design.description: The main text asks whether hierarchical extraction, calibrated intensity evaluation, controlled steering, multi-value composition, and profile alignment can be studied in one pipeline.

experimental_design.name: Rating-instability controlled comparison
experimental_design.description: For each SVT value the authors sample 10K texts and compare rating and ranking along variance, range, sign flips, prompt change, and ValueNet coherence.

experimental_design.name: HiVES training and baselines
experimental_design.description: Qwen3-embedding-0.6B is trained for 450K Stage-1 and 50K Stage-2 steps; baselines are base Qwen embedding and UniVar.

experimental_design.name: VIDB construction corpus
experimental_design.description: 32 target values use up to 10K de-duplicated texts each, target-first sampling, approximate direction balance, repeated pairwise rankings, and per-value PL.

experimental_design.name: Steering task population
experimental_design.description: The 500 queries come from GPV, ValueBench, OpinionQA, Moral Stories, and Moral Choice; there are ten named models and four theoretical frameworks / 32 values.

evidence.anchor: We evaluate ten widely used models

experimental_design.name: Prompt interventions
experimental_design.description: Intensity-anchor prompts and user-text prompts both target −2, −1, +1, +2; user text bins are specified on the VIDB scale.

experimental_design.name: Intensity evaluation protocol
experimental_design.description: The main protocol uses ranking window k=6, m=3 and Gemma-3-27B-it; Appendix Algorithm 4 fixes anchor utilities and optimizes a response utility.

experimental_design.name: Hierarchical controls
experimental_design.description: Seven-model voting accepts ≥5 agreement or a lead of ≥2; unresolved cases can be adjudicated by humans, and Neutral stops descent.

evidence.section: B.2 Details on Value Hierarchy Mapping Process

experimental_design.name: Duplicate and position-bias controls
experimental_design.description: VIDB drops exact string duplicates, randomizes focal/opponent order, and uses random swaps to evaluate judge position bias.

experimental_design.name: Demographic alignment split
experimental_design.description: Twenty-two OpinionQA demographic attributes use a 5% profile-estimation split; held-out data are reserved for downstream analyses.

experimental_design.name: Human evaluation scale
experimental_design.description: 25 evaluators provide 2,000 scalar ratings and 1,500 pairwise/windowed judgments across the covered theories.

experimental_design.name: Random seeds and decoding configuration
experimental_design.description: The PDF reports temperature robustness for OpinionQA, but does not specify random seeds, per-model decoding parameters, or query-clustering seed.

experimental_design.name: Hardware and runtime budget
experimental_design.description: Training steps, batch size, precision, and learning rates are reported; hardware type/count, wall-clock time, and memory budget are absent from the read PDF.

experimental_design.name: Human-study recruitment and adjudication protocol
experimental_design.description: The PDF gives evaluator count and task totals, but no recruitment source, compensation, demographics, IRB statement, or size of the human correction subset.

ablation_inventory.name: Prompt format and database iterations
ablation_inventory.description: Under a fixed k×m=30 budget, binary k=2 has higher pairwise ranking accuracy than default/oneshot k=5; accuracy stabilizes around m≈30.

ablation_inventory.name: Judge position bias
ablation_inventory.description: Gemma3-27b-it is selected because random left/right swaps place its choice rate closest to 0.5.

ablation_inventory.name: Evaluation K, M, judge, and sampling strategy
ablation_inventory.description: With M=3, scores stabilize at K≥4; with K=6, changes after M≥2 are typically <0.3; bucketed/fixed stabilize in 2–3 iterations and random in 4–5.

ablation_inventory.name: Latent-utility family
ablation_inventory.description: PL-6 is compared with Bradley–Terry and Thurstone under equal comparison budgets; m=3 is reported as <1 point from w=30 reference.

ablation_inventory.name: Non-prompt alternatives
ablation_inventory.description: Persona-vector and embedding-to-LLM kernel steering test whether simple activation/soft-prompt injection can replace prompt conditioning; observed control remains weak.

ablation_inventory.name: Context relevance robustness
ablation_inventory.description: Closest and farthest query-value pairs test whether semantic relevance creates the measured gains; magnitude remains similar despite different defaults.

ablation_inventory.name: Multi-turn persistence
ablation_inventory.description: A 100-turn test identifies decay toward neutral as a long-horizon boundary of one-time injection.

claim_closure.claim: A hierarchy-aware common representation can span SVT, MFT, duties, and rights.
claim_closure.origin: Introduction contribution: HiVES unifies heterogeneous theories.
claim_closure.method_response: Seven-model hierarchy mapping, cross-theory anchors, and two-stage objective.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 5 plus Appendix B similarity and hierarchy evidence.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion re-identifies hierarchical embeddings as one of three components.

claim_closure.claim: Ranking-based intensity evaluation is more stable and human-aligned than rating.
claim_closure.origin: Introduction contribution: ranking evaluation and VIDB.
claim_closure.method_response: Per-value PL, calibration, fixed-anchor ranking, plausibility/human correction.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 and Tables 14-15 directly compare stability and human judgments.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls VIDB a calibrated repository of anchors.

claim_closure.claim: Models can be steered to specified value intensities.
claim_closure.method_response: Intensity-anchor and user-text prompts with fixed-anchor evaluator.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 4/6/8 and full Appendix D curves show shifts and nonuniform failures.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion and H explicitly retain controlled-intensity trade-offs.

evidence.anchor: exact dose–response control is not always realized

claim_closure.claim: Multi-value control has asymmetric composition patterns.
claim_closure.origin: Introduction result preview and contribution result.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 8 and Figures 24-28 show additive-like and dominance/trade-off patterns.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion recalls steerability structures and composition rules.

claim_closure.claim: Value profiles improve demographic behavior prediction.
claim_closure.origin: Introduction: lightweight profiling procedure improves OpinionQA.
claim_closure.method_response: Probability/relevance-weighted group profile and prompt steering.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3 provides three model comparisons and paired t-test.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says profiling enables personalization and demographic alignment.

claim_closure.claim: The framework generalizes cross-lingually and to non-Western systems.
claim_closure.method_response: CulturaX language and corpus-driven Buddhist extension procedures.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 39-40 cover three languages and one additional system.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion names cross-cultural profiling and policy-steerable alignment.

claim_closure.claim: The three components yield scalable and reproducible infrastructure.
claim_closure.method_response: Algorithms, dataset construction, configuration table, and prompts expose key procedures.
claim_closure.evidence_response: 10 models, 32 values, 500 prompts and 50-page appendix document scope; hardware/seeds are absent.

claim_closure.claim: Exact dose-response is a general guarantee.
claim_closure.origin: Potential strong reading of controlled intensity language.
claim_closure.method_response: The method defines an approximate target relation but proves no guarantee.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Observed negative and multi-value asymmetries contradict a universal exact reading.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: H states exact dose-response is not always realized.

limitations.name: One-dimensional value-conditioned intensity
limitations.description: The conclusion states that the interface models intensity as a one-dimensional scalar conditioned on a specified value target.

limitations.name: Evaluation-call overhead
limitations.description: Ranking-based evaluation introduces additional LLM-call overhead.

limitations.name: Misuse and data/profile bias
limitations.description: Impact Statement states that steering may amplify harmful ideologies or manipulate expression, and databases/profiles may encode or reinforce bias.

evidence.anchor: could be misused to amplify harmful ideologies

limitations.name: Exact dose response and multi-value composition
limitations.description: Controlled intensities are not always exact, especially in negative directions and multi-value compositions.

evidence.anchor: exact dose–response control is not always realized

limitations.name: Coverage of values
limitations.description: The study primarily covers 32 mid-level values and calls for broader inventory including user-friendly anchors and finer sub-values.

limitations.name: Personalization at scale
limitations.description: The study does not integrate personalization at scale and names user texts, dialogue histories, preference traces, LoRA, retrieval, and hybrid profiling as future inputs.

limitations.description: These interaction settings are not fully explored.

rhetoric_analysis.interpretation: The vocabulary is driven mainly by the measurement/control mechanism rather than generic template language.

final_judgment.single_storyline: VALUEFLOW makes pluralistic value alignment operational by connecting hierarchy-aware extraction, ranking-calibrated intensity measurement, and steerable generation in one evaluator-compatible pipeline. [p.2 Figure 1; p.5 §5.1-5.2]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main text keeps the gap diagnosis, definition, three-component architecture, core loss/PL intuition, main steering figures, compressed human results, and two explicit trade-offs. [p.3; p.5-9]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A-J moves detailed literature, hierarchy construction, prompts, algorithms, calibration, full curves, qualitative examples, robustness, human-study UI, limitation, and license material. This creates a 50-page evidence dependency for per-value conclusions. [p.14-63]
final_judgment.best_pattern: Use a flow diagram to define the shared interface, a decision table to establish why the measurement choice is needed, then organize result plots by model, value, and composition. [p.2 Figure 1; p.4 Table 1; p.7-9 Figure 4/6/8]
final_judgment.largest_gap: Controlled-intensity wording exceeds a universal guarantee: no theorem or uncertainty analysis establishes exact dose response, and H records failures for negative directions and multi-value composition. [p.3 §3.1; p.63 §H]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Establish a stable, auditable measurement interface before using it to quantify an intervention; retain the decision evidence and representative failure cases in the main narrative.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule applies when credible reference anchors and a shared semantic axis exist. It cannot by itself support deployment or causal guarantees when anchors are not trustworthy, values lack interpretable coordinates, or risk requires stronger validation. [p.5 §5.2; p.63 §H]
